title: Growing squares
_map: Square patterns (stretch). Big idea: 1, 4, 9, 16: each square is the last one plus an odd number. Creative: grow a square by adding an L-shaped layer; what does each layer add?
_story: He already knows square numbers. The robot shows a way to grow a square floor in Minecraft blocks: wrap an L-shaped layer round it. Each layer adds the next odd number. A secret link between odds and squares.
_stepChain: square numbers (known) → grow 1 → 4 by adding an L → each L is a different colour → the Ls add 3, 5, 7 → odd numbers (odd-ones-out) → so squares are made of odd numbers added up → predict the 6th layer

talk.ask: How do you grow a 3 by 3 square into a 4 by 4 square?
talk.goodAnswer: add an L-shaped layer of 7 blocks round two sides.

talk.ask: What's special about the numbers each L adds?
talk.goodAnswer: they're the odd numbers in order: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.

handsOn: Build a 1 by 1, then a 2 by 2, then a 3 by 3 square with Lego, adding an L each time in a new colour. Count each L. What do you notice?

narration.speaker: robot
narration.text: You know square numbers: 1, 4, 9, 16. I'm building a square grass floor, and I want to make it bigger and bigger. Watch my trick.
Start with 1 block. Wrap an L-shape round it: 3 more blocks. Now it's a 2 by 2 square: 4. Wrap another L: 5 more blocks. Now it's 3 by 3: 9.
Now you grow it. Choose how big the square is, then tap the hammer. Each L-shaped layer is a new colour. Count the blocks in each L.
The L-shapes add 1, then 3, then 5, then 7. Those are the odd numbers! So every square number is made of odd numbers added together. 1 and 3 is 4. 1, 3 and 5 is 9.

question.prompt: How many blocks does the next L add, to make 6 by 6?
question.onRight: Yes. The odd numbers go 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, then 11. And 25 and 11 is 36.

0.hint: The L goes along two sides and round the corner.
0.say: An L covers two sides: 6 along one side and 5 more along the other. That's 11. And 25 and 11 make 36.

2.mistake: gave the new square's total instead of the L
2.hint: 36 is the whole new square. How many is the new L on its own?
2.say: 36 is the whole 6 by 6 square. The new L is the part we add: 36 take away 25 is 11.

question.reveal: The L adds 11, and 25 and 11 make 36.

rule.text: Each square is the last square plus an odd number.
rule.ask: Can you say how to grow a square, and what each L adds? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: To grow a square, add an L. Each L adds the next odd number. 1, 4, 9, 16, 25.

bonus.reveal: 64! Eight odd numbers make an 8 by 8 square. That's a Minecraft stack again!
